Create settle_bet_tx(p_bet_id UUID, p_actor_user_id UUID, p_idempotency_key TEXT, p_mode TEXT) Postgres function that runs in a single transaction

settle_bet_tx returns JSON with success, bet data, ledger_entry data, and settlement_event id

Add UNIQUE constraint on settlement_events(bet_id, settlement_version)
Enable RLS on settlement_events — SELECT policy for bookie's own records only, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies (service role only)
Create immutability trigger function prevent_mutation() that raises exception on UPDATE or DELETE
Apply prevent_mutation trigger to ledger_entries (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE)
Apply prevent_mutation trigger to settlement_events (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE)
Apply prevent_mutation trigger to audit_events (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE)
Add index on settlement_events(bet_id)
Add index on settlement_events(bookie_id, created_at)
Migration file follows existing pattern (see 006_audit_events.sql for style)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is SQL only — no edge function or Swift changes. Follow the style in supabase/migrations/006_audit_events.sql. The settle_bet_tx function should be SECURITY DEFINER so edge functions can call it via service role. Use LANGUAGE plpgsql. The payout calculation must exactly match the TypeScript in settle_bet/index.ts: win with positive odds = -(stake * (odds / 100.0)), win with negative odds = -(stake * (100.0 / abs(odds))), loss = stake, push/void = 0. Settlement description: 'Bet won', 'Bet lost', 'Bet pushed', 'Bet voided'. The settlement_events.ledger_entry_ids is a UUID array containing the single ledger entry ID created. Return JSONB from the function. See existing RPC pattern: Supabase client calls via `.rpc('settle_bet_tx', { params })`. Audit events should have entity_type='bet', action_type='settle' for the bet, and entity_type='ledger_entry', action_type='create' for the ledger row.

userStories.title: Migration: reverse_settlement_tx and override_grade_tx RPC functions
userStories.description: As a developer, I need transactional RPC functions for reversal and grade override so these correction flows cannot produce partial state.
acceptanceCriteria: Create migration file supabase/migrations/016_ledger_v2_reversal_rpcs.sql
Create reverse_settlement_tx(p_bet_id UUID, p_actor_user_id UUID, p_reason TEXT, p_idempotency_key TEXT) Postgres function

reverse_settlement_tx validates bet status is 'settled', finds most recent settlement ledger entry for the bet, then atomically: (1) creates reversal ledger entry with negated amount and type='reversal', (2) updates bet status back to 'graded', (3) inserts 2 audit_events (bet reversal + ledger entry creation), (4) returns JSON with bet, reversal_entry
Create override_grade_tx(p_bet_id UUID, p_actor_user_id UUID, p_new_outcome TEXT, p_reason TEXT, p_idempotency_key TEXT) Postgres function
override_grade_tx validates bet has non-null grade_result and new_outcome is in ('win','loss','push','void')

If bet is 'settled': override_grade_tx first performs internal reversal (same logic as reverse_settlement_tx), then updates grade_result to new_outcome, status to 'graded', emits audit events for both reversal and override
If bet is 'graded' (not settled): override_grade_tx just updates grade_result and emits override audit event
Both functions return JSONB with success flag, bet data, and any reversal entry data
Both functions are SECURITY DEFINER
If any step fails in either function, entire transaction rolls back
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow the same pattern as settle_bet_tx from migration 015. The reversal amount is: -1 * (original settlement entry amount). Find the original entry via: SELECT * FROM ledger_entries WHERE bet_id = p_bet_id AND type = 'settlement' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1. For override_grade_tx, the settled-bet path does: (1) find+reverse original settlement, (2) update bet grade_result+status, (3) audit events. The graded-only path does: (1) update bet grade_result, (2) audit event. The override does NOT re-settle — bookie must call settle_bet again.

userStories.title: Create settle_parlay edge function for server-authoritative parlay math
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a dedicated settle_parlay edge function that computes combined parlay odds and payout server-side, writing a single ledger entry for the entire parlay instead of per-leg entries.
acceptanceCriteria: Create new edge function at supabase/functions/settle_parlay/index.ts
Request: { ticket_id: string, parlay_policy: 'treatAsPush' | 'reduceLegReprice', idempotency_key: string }
Validate JWT, extract bookie, verify all bets in ticket belong to bookie
Fetch all bets with matching ticket_id, verify they share the same player_id and stake
Determine parlay outcome server-side: (1) any leg lost → LOSS, (2) all legs won → WIN, (3) apply push/void policy for mixed results
For treatAsPush policy: any push/void leg → entire parlay PUSH
For reduceLegReprice policy: exclude push/void legs, recalculate with remaining winners
Combined odds calculation: multiply decimal odds of all active legs. American to decimal: positive odds → 1 + odds/100, negative odds → 1 + 100/abs(odds)
Payout for WIN: profit = stake * combinedDecimalOdds - stake, ledger amount = -profit (bookie owes player)
Payout for LOSS: ledger amount = +stake (player owes bookie)
Payout for PUSH: ledger amount = 0
Create exactly ONE ledger entry for the whole parlay (type='settlement', description includes leg count and outcome)
Update ALL legs to status='settled' in a single batch update
Write settlement_events row with ledger_entry_ids containing the single entry ID
Emit audit event for parlay settlement with combined odds and payout in new_state
Return: { success: true, outcome: string, payout: number, ledger_entry: {...}, legs_settled: number }
Idempotency check at start, cache response at end
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Create the function directory and index.ts. Import shared helpers: cors.ts, supabase.ts, idempotency.ts, audit.ts. The ticket_id groups parlay legs — all bets with the same ticket_id are one parlay. Stake is identical on all legs (parlay convention). The key insight: instead of calling settle_bet per leg (which writes N ledger entries with per-leg odds), this writes ONE entry with the real combined payout. The description should be like 'Multi-Pick (3 legs) won' or 'Multi-Pick (3 legs) lost'. Use batch update for legs: `client.from('bets').update({ status: 'settled', updated_at: now }).in('id', legIds)`. For the settlement_events entry, use the ticket_id as a reference. This function does NOT need an RPC — it can use the single-ledger-entry approach directly since the entire operation is simpler than the per-bet case (one ledger row, one batch bet update). Deploy: `npx supabase functions deploy settle_parlay --no-verify-jwt --project-ref vstfauqufwpdytmvjyfz`.

userStories.title: Migration: hash chain columns on ledger_entries + auto-compute trigger
userStories.description: As a developer, I want tamper-evident hash chaining on ledger entries so any direct database mutation is detectable.
acceptanceCriteria: Create migration file supabase/migrations/017_ledger_v2_hash_chain.sql
Add prev_hash TEXT column to ledger_entries (nullable for first entry in a chain)
Add entry_hash TEXT NOT NULL column to ledger_entries
Create compute_ledger_hash() trigger function that fires BEFORE INSERT on ledger_entries
Trigger looks up the most recent entry_hash for the same (bookie_id, player_id) pair ordered by created_at DESC
Sets prev_hash to that value (NULL if no previous entry exists)
Computes entry_hash = encode(sha256(concat(coalesce(prev_hash,''), bookie_id::text, player_id::text, amount::text, type, created_at::text, NEW.id::text)::bytea), 'hex')
The trigger sets NEW.prev_hash and NEW.entry_hash before the row is inserted
Backfill existing ledger_entries: run a DO block that iterates entries per (bookie_id, player_id) ordered by created_at ASC and computes the chain
After backfill, add NOT NULL constraint to entry_hash (prev_hash stays nullable for chain heads)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The hash chain is scoped per (bookie_id, player_id) — each player under each bookie has their own independent chain. The trigger must use FOR UPDATE locking on the previous entry lookup to prevent race conditions with concurrent inserts. Use: SELECT entry_hash FROM ledger_entries WHERE bookie_id = NEW.bookie_id AND player_id = NEW.player_id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE. For the backfill, iterate with a cursor or nested loop: FOR each distinct (bookie_id, player_id), FOR each entry ordered by created_at ASC, compute and UPDATE. This is the one time we update ledger_entries — the immutability trigger from US-001 must be temporarily disabled during backfill (use ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER prevent_mutation_ledger_entries, then re-enable).

userStories.title: Create validate_ledger_chain RPC function
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a Postgres function that validates the hash chain for any player's ledger so tampering is detectable on demand.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Postgres function validate_ledger_chain(p_bookie_id UUID, p_player_id UUID) in migration 017 or a new 018 migration
Function iterates all ledger_entries for (bookie_id, player_id) ordered by created_at ASC
For each entry, recomputes expected hash using same formula as the insertion trigger
Verifies: (1) entry_hash matches recomputed hash, (2) prev_hash matches previous entry's entry_hash, (3) chain head has prev_hash IS NULL
Returns JSONB: { valid: boolean, entries_checked: integer, first_invalid_entry_id: uuid | null, error_message: text | null }
If all entries match, returns { valid: true, entries_checked: N }
If mismatch found, returns { valid: false, first_invalid_entry_id: <id>, error_message: 'Hash mismatch at entry <id>' }
Function is SECURITY DEFINER so edge functions can call it
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is a read-only validation function. Use a FOR loop over the cursor with a running prev_hash variable. Start with prev_hash = NULL. For each row: compute expected_hash using the same concat+sha256+hex formula, compare with stored entry_hash, compare prev_hash with running value. If any mismatch, record the entry ID and break. This can be called on-demand from an edge function or as a scheduled job. No edge function wrapper needed yet — direct RPC call from client or admin tools.

userStories.title: Create player_balances_view and get_player_balance RPC
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a canonical server-side balance computation so reports and reconciliation use authoritative values rather than client-derived math.
acceptanceCriteria: Create migration file supabase/migrations/018_ledger_v2_canonical_balances.sql (or append to 017)
Create VIEW player_balances_view AS SELECT bookie_id, player_id, COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) as balance_owed FROM ledger_entries GROUP BY bookie_id, player_id
Create get_player_balance(p_bookie_id UUID, p_player_id UUID) Postgres function
Function returns JSONB: { balance_owed: numeric, open_stakes: numeric, available_credit: numeric }
balance_owed = SUM of all ledger_entries.amount for (bookie_id, player_id)
open_stakes = SUM of stake from bets WHERE bookie_id matches AND player_id matches AND status IN ('pending', 'accepted')
available_credit = player.credit_limit - open_stakes - balance_owed (lookup credit_limit from players table)
Function is SECURITY DEFINER
Enable RLS on the view — bookies can only see their own players' balances
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The view is a convenience for dashboards and reports. The RPC function is the canonical balance endpoint. The balance formula mirrors BalanceService.swift exactly: availableCredit = creditLimit - openStakes - balanceOwed. Internal convention: positive balance_owed = player owes bookie. The players table has a credit_limit column. Open stakes only include pending + accepted bets (not graded, settled, void, declined). This provides the 'server says' value that the iOS client can reconcile against.
